fields.label: Spasticity (Modified Ashworth Scale), most affected group
opts: 1: Slight increase, catch and release or minimal resistance at the end of the range
1+: Slight increase, catch then minimal resistance through less than half the range
2: More marked increase through most of the range, but part easily moved

fields.hint: e.g. right elbow flexors 1+, right ankle plantar flexors 2

sections.title: Red flags
sections.alert: Red flag present. New neurological deficit, reduced consciousness or seizure: stop therapy and arrange emergency medical assessment now (possible stroke, bleed or cord compression). Suspected DVT: pause lower-limb exercise, apply the two-level Wells score and arrange a proximal leg vein ultrasound, ideally within 4 hours. Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or haemoptysis: emergency assessment for pulmonary embolism.

fields.label: New or worsening weakness, numbness, facial droop, speech or vision problem
New bladder or bowel disturbance or saddle numbness
Reduced consciousness, sudden severe headache or new seizure
Calf pain, swelling, warmth or redness in one leg (suspected DVT)
Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or coughing blood

advice.title: Your home exercise programme
advice.text: Do the exercises you have been shown every day, a little at a time, and rest if the pain becomes sharp or much worse. Use your walking aid, brace or splint exactly as shown. Practise everyday tasks such as washing and dressing yourself as much as you safely can: regular practice between sessions helps recovery.

advice.title: Signs of a blood clot
advice.text: Come to hospital at once if one leg becomes painful, swollen, warm or red, or if you suddenly feel breathless, have chest pain or cough up blood.

advice.title: New weakness: come at once
advice.text: Call an ambulance or come to hospital at once if you notice new weakness or numbness of the face, arm or leg, slurred speech, loss of vision, a sudden severe headache, a fit, or new difficulty passing urine or stools.
